name: solid
description: A declarative, efficient, and flexible JavaScript library for building user interfaces.
readmeHtml:
Website • Docs • Tutorial • Playground • Discord

Solid is a declarative JavaScript library for building user interfaces. Instead of a Virtual DOM, it compiles templates to real DOM nodes and updates them with fine-grained reactivity. Declare your state and use it throughout your app — when a piece of state changes, only the code that depends on it re-runs.

At a glance

import { createSignal } from "solid-js";
import { render } from "@solidjs/web";

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0);
  const doubled = () => count() * 2;

  // The component body runs once. Only `{doubled()}` updates when count changes.
  return <button onClick={() => setCount(c => c + 1)}>{doubled()}</button>;
}

render(() => <Counter />, document.getElementById("app")!);

Try it in our Playground.

Explain this!

Solid compiles your JSX to real DOM operations at build time. The component function runs once on mount; reactivity is per-expression, not per-render. The {doubled()} expression compiles to a tracked update that only touches that one DOM position when count() changes.

import { template, delegateEvents, insert } from "@solidjs/web";
import { createSignal } from "solid-js";

const _tmpl$ = /*#__PURE__*/ template(`<button>`);

function Counter() {
  const [count, setCount] = createSignal(0);
  const doubled = () => count() * 2;

  return (() => {
    const _el$ = _tmpl$();
    _el$._$$click = () => setCount(c => c + 1);
    insert(_el$, doubled);
    return _el$;
  })();
}
delegateEvents(["click"]);

Reads update on the next microtask (or call flush() for synchronous interop). Effects are split into a tracking compute phase and a side-effecting apply phase — see the docs for the full model.

Key features

  • Fine-grained updates to the real DOM — no virtual DOM diff.
  • Declarative reactive primitives (createSignal, createMemo, createStore).
  • Render-once components — your component function is plain JavaScript that runs once.
  • Automatic dependency tracking — reading reactive state subscribes to it.
  • Microtask-batched updates with flush() for synchronous interop.
  • First-class async: any computation can return a Promise/AsyncIterable; <Loading> is the boundary.
  • Optimistic UI primitives (createOptimistic, createOptimisticStore) and structured action(...) mutations.
  • Streaming SSR and progressive hydration.
  • TypeScript-first, JSX-first, web-component friendly.
  • Universal: write custom renderers via @solidjs/universal to target non-DOM platforms.

Quick start

Start from a template:

npx degit solidjs/templates/solid-v2/basic my-app
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev

Or add Solid to an existing Vite project:

npm i solid-js @solidjs/web
npm i -D vite @solidjs/vite-plugin
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import solid from "@solidjs/vite-plugin";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [solid()]
});

and point TypeScript at the web JSX types:

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "jsx": "preserve",
    "jsxImportSource": "@solidjs/web"
  }
}

solid-js owns renderer-neutral component types, while renderer packages such as @solidjs/web and @solidjs/h own their JSX namespaces and jsx-runtime type entries.

Coming from Solid 1.x?

Read the migration guide. Solid 1.x is maintained on the 1.x branch, installs with npm i solid-js@v1-latest, and its docs are at v1.solidjs.com.

For LLMs / AI assistants

The public API differs from any Solid examples that predate 2.0. Before generating Solid 2.0 code, read:

  • packages/solid/skills/solid-2.0/SKILL.md — the primer: the three rules that matter most, the 1.x → 2.0 corrections, and the primitives to reach for, in under 8 KB.
  • packages/solid/CHEATSHEET.md — one-page reference; the bottom enumerates patterns that changed from 1.x.
  • documentation/solid-2.0/MIGRATION.md — full migration guide.
  • docs.solidjs.com — the docs, with /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt.

The primer and the cheatsheet ship inside the solid-js npm package (node_modules/solid-js/skills/solid-2.0/SKILL.md, node_modules/solid-js/CHEATSHEET.md; the build also emits the cheatsheet as the solid-2.0-cheatsheet skill). The packages carry the tanstack-intent keyword, so skill registries that scan node_modules find them.

Repository

This is a PNPM workspaces monorepo. The core runtime (solid-js, @solidjs/signals, @solidjs/web, @solidjs/universal, @solidjs/diagnostics) always shares one version. The two compilers share a version when they release together, and @solidjs/h, @solidjs/html and @solidjs/element version on their own.

Package Path Purpose
solid-js packages/solid Core runtime — components, flow controls, context, hydration.
@solidjs/signals packages/signals Reactive primitives — signals, memos, effects, stores.
@solidjs/web packages/web Web platform runtime — render, hydrate, SSR, Portal, dynamic.
@solidjs/h packages/h Hyperscript / JSX factory.
@solidjs/html packages/html Build-less tagged template literals.
@solidjs/universal packages/universal Universal runtime for custom renderers.
@solidjs/element packages/element Web Components wrapper.
@solidjs/compiler packages/compiler Native Oxc JSX compiler.
@solidjs/babel-plugin packages/babel-plugin Babel plugin for JSX compilation.
@solidjs/diagnostics packages/diagnostics Dev-only diagnostics and attribution harness for tests and agents.

Runtime DOM operations live in @solidjs/web (and @solidjs/universal / @solidjs/h / @solidjs/html). The JSX compilers and the DOM runtime live in this repo, so file their issues here, not on DOM Expressions. The API reference in one page is packages/solid/CHEATSHEET.md, and the design notes are under documentation/solid-2.0/.

Why Solid?

Performant

Engineered for performance with years of research behind it — Solid's runtime cost is close to optimized vanilla JavaScript on the JS Framework Benchmark. Small, fully tree-shakable, fast on the server too. (Read more about Solid's performance.)

Powerful

Performant state management is built in (Context, Stores, Projections). Async is a first-class capability of computations, with <Loading> / <Errored> boundaries and isPending for revalidation indicators. Full SSR, streaming, and progressive hydration when you're ready to move to the server.

Pragmatic

Components are plain functions. Rendering is determined by how state is used — no rendering system to learn. Read-write segregation is encouraged but not enforced.

Productive

Built on JSX and TypeScript, integrates with the Vite ecosystem. Bare-metal abstractions give you direct access to the DOM. Growing ecosystem of primitives, component libraries, and build-time utilities.

More

  • Documentation
  • Tutorial
  • Examples
  • Playground

Browser support

SolidJS Core supports the last 2 years of modern Firefox, Safari, Chrome, and Edge (desktop and mobile). IE and similar sunset browsers are not supported. For server environments, Node LTS, the latest Deno, and Cloudflare Worker runtimes are supported.

Community

Come chat on Discord. Solid's maintainers are active there, and we're always looking for contributions.

Contributors

Open Collective

Support us with a donation and help us continue our activities. [Contribute]

Sponsors

Become a sponsor and get your logo on our README on GitHub with a link to your site. [Become a sponsor]

releases.name: solid-js@2.0.4
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- fcaa051: Stop serializing synchronous `createProjection` / `createOptimisticStore` derives that only waited on a pending async source during SSR, so hydrated projections run live against their hydrated source and follow subsequent writes (#5146).
- a406a5d: Hydrating a settled promise of an async iterable whose stream already yielded more than once now claims the first value, as a direct stream does, instead of a later one. A stream, direct or behind a settled promise, that threw after its first yield now claims that first value and then shows the `<Errored>` fallback, instead of failing inside the claim pass and leaving the server's content on screen.
- 8bfca0d: Docs: the `createOptimistic`, `createOptimisticStore` and `action` JSDoc now say that optimistic writes always revert when the action settles, and their examples keep the result by refreshing or writing the source of truth. The previous examples kept nothing (#5129).
- f353760: Ship the MIT `LICENSE` file in the fixed-group package roots (`solid-js`, `@solidjs/web`, and the same-release `@solidjs/universal` / `@solidjs/diagnostics`) so npm tarballs include the license text for third-party notice genera

releases.name: @solidjs/web@2.0.4
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- c66e1cc: The JSX types for MathML attributes whose values are the strings `"true"` and `"false"` (`displaystyle`, `stretchy`, `largeop`, `movablelimits`, `symmetric`, `fence`, `separator`, `accent`, `accentunder`) now accept those strings and reject `{true}`, the bare attribute and `""`, which write an empty value that MathML ignores, as well as `boolean`-typed values. `{false}` still removes the attribute.
- 21822b2: An empty `revalidate` declaration (`[]` or `""`) is now sent as `X-Revalidate: ,` instead of an empty header value, which intermediaries such as CDNs drop, turning "revalidate nothing" into "revalidate everything".
- 0791152: Navigating a frame to an address whose server render throws now shows the error in the nearest `<Errored>` and drops `isPending`, instead of keeping the previous content up while pending forever: the server sends that response's `:error` and `:complete` as one batch, and the landing now rejects on it.
- 6d3cdef: The dev-mode hydration tag check reads the template's full tag name, so a correctly claimed custom element (a tag with a hyphen) no longer warns `Hydration tag mismatch`.
- f353760: Ship the MIT `LICENSE` file in the

releases.name: @solidjs/universal@2.0.4
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- f5252dd: A custom renderer's single-child hole now mounts content that arrives during a held action at the commit, like `@solidjs/web` does, instead of showing a bare element before it.
- b7d939f: Ship the MIT `LICENSE` file in every published package (#5106).
- ef08c1e: A prop whose expression is a ternary over an async source (`n={ans() == null ? -1 : ans().length}`) now reads the value on screen from an event handler while the source re-asks, instead of throwing `NotReadyError`. Called with no owner (an event handler, an effect callback), the compiled `memo` helper returns its function instead of creating a memo, so an effect callback that reads such a prop no longer reports `PRIMITIVE_IN_EFFECT_CALLBACK` in dev. A template created with no owner therefore has no condition memo: its conditional rebuilds the branch each time the condition's sources change, not only when the condition flips.
- 842144c: Pass numeric text children to the renderer's `createTextNode` and `replaceText` as strings.
- Updated dependencies [fcaa051]

releases.name: @solidjs/signals@2.0.4
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- 543066e: A store array that an action replaces with a returned array, then pushes to after a `yield`, now maps the pushed row in `mapArray` and `<For>` instead of `undefined` (#5093).
- 83d42ba: Allow calling an action from a cleanup during teardown, as #4165 allowed writes. Removing a keyed row ran its cleanups inside the list's pass, so an action invoked from an `onCleanup` or an effect's returned cleanup threw `ACTION_CALLED_IN_OWNED_SCOPE` in development, while the same cleanup under a branch switching away ran. The dev-only action guard now stands down while cleanups run, like the owned-scope write guard. Production builds are unchanged.
- 30e7805: A cleanup that runs while a transition lands and writes a node that transition still holds no longer evicts another live transition (its `isPending` stayed `true` forever) or folds a live transition into the landed one (#5159).
- 21bfd2d: Coalesce synchronous subscription bursts in `from()` before settling a pending pull.
- 3774ebe: A declined optimistic edit now reverts in a list row that a `Show` is about to replace, at the same moment as everywhere else (#5077). Before, when the frame that would remove the ol

releases.name: @solidjs/html@2.0.2
releases.body:
### Patch Changes

- c74567a: Clarify how to write a literal less-than sign in tagged JSX text when a tag start is invalid.
- ebe4cf3: Render spread and explicit children props on native elements with no template children.
- eca83db: Keep nested template renders from interrupting traversal of the outer template.
- 4805dea: Let nested component children override an explicit children prop, including function-valued props.
- 41b4b7e: Preserve whitespace-only content and normalize an initial newline in pre and textarea elements.
- bab8a53: Preserve character references literally in HTML script and style raw text.
- cad0143: Preserve literal markup in textarea and title text while decoding character references.
- 4238d2d: Reject table rows directly under a table, matching the JSX compiler's malformed HTML validation.
- b7d939f: Ship the MIT `LICENSE` file in every published package (#5106).

aiSummary.oneLiner: Fine‑grained reactive core that compiles JSX to direct DOM updates, eliminating the virtual DOM
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Solid solves the performance overhead of virtual‑DOM diffing by compiling JSX templates into real DOM operations at build time. It introduces fine‑grained reactivity where each reactive expression tracks its own dependencies and only re‑executes when those specific values change. The component function runs once, and updates are applied through microtask‑batched effects, giving near‑vanilla JavaScript speed. Its API is TypeScript‑first and works with any renderer via @solidjs/universal, making it suitable for web, SSR, and custom platforms.
keyFeatures: Fine-grained updates: only the DOM nodes that depend on changed signals are patched
Declarative primitives: createSignal, createMemo, and createStore provide reactive state without boilerplate
Render‑once components: component functions execute a single time and never re‑render
Microtask batching: flush() allows synchronous interop while default updates are batched in microtasks
Streaming SSR & progressive hydration: supports server‑side rendering with incremental client hydration

useCases.title: High‑performance web apps
useCases.description: Developers building interactive dashboards or games need sub‑millisecond UI updates; Solid’s granular reactivity delivers that without a virtual DOM.

useCases.title: Server‑side rendering with hydration
useCases.description: Teams requiring SEO‑friendly pages can use Solid’s streaming SSR and progressive hydration to send HTML first and hydrate only when needed.

useCases.title: Component library authoring
useCases.description: Library authors benefit from plain‑function components and renderer‑agnostic core, enabling creation of UI kits that work in React‑like environments and custom renderers.

useCases.title: TypeScript‑heavy codebases
useCases.description: Projects that rely on strict typing gain from Solid’s TypeScript‑first design, ensuring compile‑time safety for reactive primitives and JSX.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Frontend engineers who want maximum runtime performance and are comfortable with JSX and TypeScript. It assumes familiarity with reactive programming concepts and a build tool like Vite or similar.
